topics.title: Tables & Data Semantics
topics.summary: Represent genuinely tabular data with captions, header cells, row/column scope, and a structure that remains understandable to assistive technology.

concepts.name: Table anatomy
concepts.explanation: table contains rows. thead, tbody, and tfoot group row regions; tr is a row, th is a header cell, and td is a data cell.

concepts.name: Headers and scope
concepts.explanation: Use th for headers and scope="col" or scope="row" when the relationship is not obvious. These relationships help screen readers announce context.

concepts.name: Use tables for data
concepts.explanation: Tables are for data relationships, not page layout. CSS Grid and Flexbox are the correct tools for general visual layout.

topics.title: Audio, Video & Timed Tracks
topics.summary: Embed media with native controls, fallbacks, captions, and multiple sources where useful.

concepts.name: Native media
concepts.explanation: audio and video can expose built-in controls with the controls attribute. Browsers can select from multiple source elements.

concepts.name: Captions and subtitles
concepts.explanation: track can provide captions, subtitles, descriptions, chapters, or metadata using WebVTT files. Captions are important for accessibility.

concepts.name: Fallbacks and preload
concepts.explanation: Provide fallback text or links when media cannot play. preload is a hint; do not assume the browser will always download exactly as requested.

topics.challenge: Create a video element with controls, at least one source, and a captions track.
topics.hint: The important nesting is video → source/track/fallback content.

topics.title: Advanced Forms & Native Validation
topics.summary: Use richer input types, grouping, autocomplete, constraint attributes, and accessible error-friendly structure before adding JavaScript.

concepts.name: Constraint attributes
concepts.explanation: required, minlength, maxlength, min, max, step, and pattern let browsers reject many invalid values without custom JavaScript.

concepts.name: Grouping controls
concepts.explanation: fieldset groups related controls and legend gives the group a name. This is especially helpful for radio buttons and related checkboxes.

concepts.name: Autocomplete
concepts.explanation: autocomplete tokens help browsers and password managers understand what a field represents. Correct tokens can improve both speed and accessibility.

topics.example:
<form>
  <fieldset>
    <legend>Notification preference</legend>
    <label><input type="radio" name="notice" value="email" required> Email</label>
    <label><input type="radio" name="notice" value="sms"> SMS</label>
  </fieldset>
  <label for="age">Age</label>
  <input id="age" name="age" type="number" min="13" max="120" required>
  <button>Continue</button>
</form>
topics.challenge: Build a form that uses fieldset/legend and at least two native validation attributes.
topics.hint: Use required plus a type-specific constraint such as min/max, minlength, or pattern.
topics.solution:
<form>
  <fieldset>
    <legend>Notification preference</legend>
    <label><input type="radio" name="notice" value="email" required> Email</label>
    <label><input type="radio" name="notice" value="sms"> SMS</label>
  </fieldset>
  <label for="age">Age</label>
  <input id="age" name="age" type="number" min="13" max="120" required>
  <button>Continue</button>
</form>

topics.title: Metadata, SEO & Document Head
topics.summary: Use the head to describe encoding, viewport behavior, page identity, canonical resources, stylesheets, icons, and metadata for sharing/search.

concepts.name: Essential metadata
concepts.explanation: charset should appear early. viewport metadata is important for mobile layout. title gives each document a meaningful browser/tab and search result label.

concepts.name: Links and relationships
concepts.explanation: link can connect stylesheets, icons, canonical URLs, preloads, and other related resources to the document.

concepts.name: Descriptions and robots
concepts.explanation: meta name="description" can summarize the page for search results. Robots directives influence indexing but are not a security mechanism.

topics.example:
<head>
  <meta charset="utf-8">
  <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">
  <title>HTML Junior — Code Ascension</title>
  <meta name="description" content="Study HTML Junior lessons and class tests.">
  <link rel="stylesheet" href="styles.css">
  <link rel="icon" href="favicon.svg" type="image/svg+xml">
</head>
topics.challenge: Write a head section with charset, viewport, title, description and stylesheet link.
topics.hint: Metadata belongs inside head, not body. Treat the title and description as user-facing content.
topics.solution:
<head>
  <meta charset="utf-8">
  <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">
  <title>HTML Junior — Code Ascension</title>
  <meta name="description" content="Study HTML Junior lessons and class tests.">
  <link rel="stylesheet" href="styles.css">
  <link rel="icon" href="favicon.svg" type="image/svg+xml">
</head>

topics.title: Responsive Images & Art Direction
topics.summary: Serve appropriate images for different pixel densities, viewport sizes, and compositions with srcset, sizes, picture, and source.

concepts.name: Resolution switching
concepts.explanation: srcset can offer multiple image widths or pixel densities. sizes describes the displayed width so the browser can choose an efficient candidate.

concepts.name: Art direction
concepts.explanation: picture and source let you provide different crops or formats for different conditions rather than merely resizing the same composition.

concepts.name: Fallback image
concepts.explanation: picture still ends with an img element. That img supplies the fallback source and the alt text for the image as a whole.

topics.challenge: Create a responsive image using picture/source and an img fallback with srcset or sizes.
topics.hint: The img element is still required at the end of picture and owns the alt text.
